title: Asymmetric Cyanosilylation of Aldehydes by a Lewis Acid/Base Synergistic Catalyst of Chiral Metal Clusters

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.compound_name: S-enantiomer of the cobalt–terbium chiral cluster

synthesis.procedure: CoCl2·6H2O and TbCl3·6H2O were dissolved in MeOH/EtOH. The previously prepared (S)-L1 Schiff-base ligand solution and triethylamine were added. The mixture was stirred for 2 h at room temperature, transferred to a beaker, and allowed to evaporate under atmospheric conditions. Red block crystals formed after 1 week.
synthesis.vessel_or_method: solution stirring followed by evaporation in a 25 mL beaker
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Evaporation under atmospheric conditions yielded red block crystals.

properties.summary: The enantiomeric terbium clusters give nearly mirror-image circular-dichroism spectra, consistent with their opposite chirality. UV–visible spectra were also discussed.

measurements.name: circular-dichroism signal
measurements.conditions: CD spectrum in N,N-dimethylformamide; peaks reported for the (R)/(S)-Co3Tb2 pair

source_locations.location: Experimental Section, Synthesis of Chiral Metal Clusters

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.structure_description: The article describes the isostructural Co3Ln2 clusters using (R)-Co3Tb2 as the representative: a twisted triangular metal core with three Co ions at vertices and two Tb ions at side midpoints, protected by chiral Schiff-base and amino-diol ligands. The (S) and (R) terbium structures are mirror images.

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.compound_name: R-enantiomer of the cobalt–terbium chiral cluster

synthesis.procedure: Prepared by the stated procedure for (S)-Co3Tb2, replacing the (S)-L1 ligand solution with the previously prepared (R)-L1 solution: CoCl2·6H2O and TbCl3·6H2O in MeOH/EtOH were treated with ligand and triethylamine, stirred at room temperature for 2 h, and evaporated under atmospheric conditions for approximately 1 week.
synthesis.vessel_or_method: solution stirring followed by evaporation in a 25 mL beaker
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Crystals obtained by evaporation under atmospheric conditions.

properties.summary: The enantiomeric terbium clusters give nearly mirror-image circular-dichroism spectra, consistent with their opposite chirality. UV–visible spectra were also discussed.

measurements.name: circular-dichroism signal
measurements.conditions: CD spectrum in N,N-dimethylformamide; peaks reported for the (R)/(S)-Co3Tb2 pair

source_locations.location: Experimental Section, Synthesis of Chiral Metal Clusters

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.structure_description: The representative crystal structure has a twisted triangular Co3Tb2 metal core, with three Co(III) ions at the vertices and two Tb(III) ions at side midpoints. Two trideprotonated (R)-L1, three dideprotonated (R)-L1, and one deprotonated (R)-L2 ligand protect the cationic cluster; chloride counterions and guest water accompany it.

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.compound_name: S-enantiomer of the cobalt–dysprosium chiral cluster

synthesis.procedure: Prepared under the stated (S)-Co3Tb2 conditions, replacing TbCl3·6H2O with DyCl3·6H2O. The metal salts in MeOH/EtOH were treated with (S)-L1 ligand solution and triethylamine, stirred at room temperature for 2 h, and left to evaporate under atmospheric conditions.

reagents.name: dysprosium(III) chloride hexahydrate
reagents.amount: 0.1 mmol under the stated identical conditions

synthesis.time: 2 h stirring; approximately 1 week evaporation under the stated identical conditions
synthesis.vessel_or_method: solution stirring followed by evaporation in a 25 mL beaker
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Crystals obtained by evaporation under atmospheric conditions.

properties.summary: Circular-dichroism spectra of the dysprosium enantiomers were reported to be similar to those of the terbium pair and to show opposite chiral responses. UV–visible spectra were also discussed.

source_locations.location: Experimental Section, Synthesis of Chiral Metal Clusters

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.structure_description: The paper identifies this as the dysprosium analogue of the isostructural chiral Co3Ln2 family. Its five-metal cluster contains three Co and two Dy ions and is supported by chiral Schiff-base-derived ligands.

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.compound_name: R-enantiomer of the cobalt–dysprosium chiral cluster

synthesis.procedure: Prepared under the stated conditions for the terbium clusters, using (R)-L1 instead of (S)-L1 and DyCl3·6H2O instead of TbCl3·6H2O. The metal salts in MeOH/EtOH were treated with ligand and triethylamine, stirred at room temperature for 2 h, and left to evaporate under atmospheric conditions.

synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Crystals obtained by evaporation under atmospheric conditions.
